instruments.label: Big-tech backstop (guarantee + warrants)
instruments.pricing_rule_of_thumb: backstop $ size implies ~0.3-0.5x that dollar amount in warrant value at the observed Google/Cipher ratio (~$1.73B total backstop for ~5.4%+ equity of a company valued in the low billions) -- backstops are priced as expensive but bankable credit enhancement, not free insurance

credit_rating_mapping.note: no public corporate ratings exist for Core Scientific, Cipher, TeraWulf, IREN, Hut 8, or Applied Digital individually -- they access capital via project-level secured debt/converts, not a rated corporate structure. CoreWeave is the outlier: S&P 'B+' issuer rating (Positive outlook), with DDTL 4.0 achieving the sector's first investment-grade-rated GPU-backed financing (A3/A-low) despite the corporate rating staying at B+ -- i.e. structured/secured debt can be rated far above the parent when backlog quality is strong.
credit_rating_mapping.backlog_quality_definition: weak = mostly unrated/AI-lab tenants, no backstop; mixed = blend; strong = mostly hyperscaler/IG tenants, backstopped
credit_rating_mapping.source: recommended mapping, derived from the CoreWeave pattern -- confirmed as the game value
